Senses.Explanation: The Baizhang-revisits-Mazu of the Chan records: the whisk raised and hung back, this use or away from this use, the awesomely-roared shout — three days deaf, Huangbo's tongue out. Xueyan Zuqin opens his hall: my way is wondrous hard to think, and beyond words besides — Baizhang's second visit to Mazu: one shout, three days deaf, outright enough to make Huangbo put out his tongue. He raises his own whisk: what has it to do with it? Xiaoyin Daxin raises it at the central Tianzhu hall: Mazu eyes the whisk at the bed-corner — this use, or away from this use? — hung back in the old place; and later, with what will you teach others? — Baizhang takes the whisk and raises it; this use, or away from this use? — hung back again — the shout, three days deaf outright — and his own grading: seizing mechanism with mechanism, breaking the target with the target — Baizhang himself struck three days deaf, Huangbo later startled tongue-out, Yuejiang Zhengyin releases the retreat: one stone dragged, two loads of earth carried, the trigger must be a thousand-jun crossbow — yet the thousand-jun crossbow does not trigger for a shrew-mouse — Baizhang's second visit to Mazu: the awesomely-roared shout, three days deaf outright; Linji reaching Dayu and at once saying Huangbo's way's-law has not much to it, Gaoting seeing Deshan across the river — a beckon, a slanting dash — Xuansha before Xuefeng rolling the three wooden balls into the sign-board-splitting stance: all with the cheep-and-peck same-moment eye and its same-moment use, and Yu'an Zhiji verses it: the on-the-spot shout like thunder — who says the refined-gold color does not return? Deaf ears and tongue out together — the armor of the three mysteries planted in fire. Wuming Huijing takes the Emei-peak ask whole: the whisk raised — this use, away from this use; hung back, the awesomely-roared shout, three days deaf — and after the deafness, what did he get? Pah! What the old man Shakyamuni handed Kasyapa. His verse: the thousand-jun crossbow is not for a shrew-mouse; one raised edge subdues the lion's might; dragon-elephant onlookers feel heart and gall shatter — a thing rare in world and heaven, Lianfeng Su comes back to his mountain: leaving it, straw sandals fierce as a tiger; returning — nothing like Baizhang's second visit to Mazu; how about Fenggan journeying far to bow at Wutai? The one thing most wondrous: those met are all people of the old days, eyebrows still planted above the eyes, all re-gathered, sitting where the cold ashes blaze — do not fail, in frost and snow, the one cold plum branch, and Zhulang Chesheng verses it: one shout like thunder, the sand-realm emptied; common feeling and holy reading fused in a moment; since the day both ears went deaf — down to today, never once sharp-eared.
